arxiv-1904-02152.title: 459SolvDynSystPlaneWithPolynInteract190122
arxiv-1904-02152.creator: (Submitted to: J. Phys. Conf. Ser., 22.01.2019)
arxiv-1904-02152.description: Abstract We tersely review a recently introduced technique to identify systems of two nonlinearly-coupled Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) solvable by algebraic operations ; and we report some specific examples of this kind, namely systems of 2 first-order ODEs with polynomial right-hand sides, \dot{x}_{n}=P^{\left(n\right)}\left(x_{1},x_{2}\right)~,~~~n=1,2~, satisfied by the 2 (possibly complex ) dependent variables x_{n}\equiv x_{n}\left(t\right) .

arxiv-2110-14878.creator: T. Aaltonen, S. Amerio ll, D. Amidei, A. Anastassov w, A. Annovi, J. Antos, G. Apollinari, J.A. Appel, T. Arisawa, A. Artikov, J. Asaadi, W. Ashmanskas, B. Auerbach, A. Aurisano, F. Azfar, W. Badgett, T. Bae, A. Barbaro-Galtieri, V.E. Barnes, B.A. Barnett, P. Barria nn, P. Bartos, M. Bauce ll, F. Be
arxiv-2110-14878.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by T. Aaltonen, S. Amerio ll, D. Amidei, A. Anastassov w, A. Annovi, J. Antos, G. Apollinari, J.A. Appel, T. Arisawa, A. Artikov, J. Asaadi, W. Ashmanskas, B. Auerbach, A. Aurisano, F. Azfar, W. Badgett, T. Bae, A. Barbaro-Galtieri, V.E. Barnes, B.A. Barnett, P. Barria nn, P. Bartos, M. Bauce ll, F. Be. A study of initial-state gluon radiation (ISR) in hadron collisions is presented using Drell-Yan (DY) events produced in proton-antiproton collisions by the Tevatron collider at a center-of-mass energy of 1.96 TeV.

arxiv-2205-11850.title: Faithful Explanations for Deep Graph Models
arxiv-2205-11850.creator: Zifan Wang, Yuhang Yao, Chaoran Zhang, Han Zhang, Youjie Kang
arxiv-2205-11850.description: Abstract This paper studies faithful explanations for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). First, we provide a new and general method for formally characterizing the faithfulness of explanations for GNNs. It applies to existing explanation methods, including feature attributions and subgraph explanations.

arxiv-2206-08482.title: GMI-DRL: Empowering Multi-GPU Deep Reinforcement Learning with GPU Spatial Multiplexing
arxiv-2206-08482.creator: Yuke Wang, Boyuan Feng, Zheng Wang, Tong Geng, Ang Li, and Yufei Ding{yuke_wang, boyuan, zheng_wang, yufeiding}@cs.ucsb.eduUniversity of California, Santa Barbara
arxiv-2206-08482.description: Abstract With the increasing popularity of robotics in industrial control and autonomous driving, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) raises the attention of various fields. However, DRL computation on the modern powerful GPU platform is still inefficient due to its heterogeneous workloads and interleaved execution paradigm.

arxiv-2207-12189.title: Encoded State Transfer: Beyond the Uniform Chain
arxiv-2207-12189.creator: Alastair Kay
arxiv-2207-12189.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alastair Kay. In a recent work Kay 2022 , we showed that a uniformly coupled chain could be symmetrically extended by engineered spin chains in such a way that we could choose part of the spectrum of the overall system. When combined with an encoding that avoids the uncontrolled eigenvalues, this resulted in the possibility of achieving a range of tasks such as perfect quantum state transfer.

arxiv-2305-19374.title: Compositional diversity in visual concept learning
arxiv-2305-19374.creator: Yanli Zhou, Reuben Feinman, Brenden M. Lake
arxiv-2305-19374.description: Abstract Humans leverage compositionality to efficiently learn new concepts, understanding how familiar parts can combine together to form novel objects. In contrast, popular computer vision models struggle to make the same types of inferences, requiring more data and generalizing less flexibly than people do.

arxiv-2403-13621.title: Importance of accounting for student identities and intersectionality for creating equitable and inclusive physics learning environments
arxiv-2403-13621.creator: Lisabeth Marie Santana, Chandralekha Singh
arxiv-2403-13621.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lisabeth Marie Santana, Chandralekha Singh. This research focuses on the experiences of seven undergraduate women who were majoring in physics in a medium-size physics department at a small liberal arts college. In the semi-structured, empathetic interviews we conducted, the women discussed how they decided to major in physics, their interactions with their peers and instructors, who supported them during their physics trajectory, and suggestions that would improve their experiences in physics.

arxiv-2404-07779.title: Improving Network Degree Correlation by Degree-preserving Rewiring
arxiv-2404-07779.creator: Shuo Zou, Bo Zhou, and Qi Xuan
arxiv-2404-07779.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shuo Zou, Bo Zhou, and Qi Xuan. Degree correlation is a crucial measure in networks, significantly impacting network topology and dynamical behavior. The degree sequence of a network is a significant characteristic, and altering network degree correlation through degree-preserving rewiring poses an interesting problem. In this paper, we define the problem of maximizing network degree correlation through a finite number of rewirings and use the assortativity coefficient to measure it.

arxiv-2404-17518.title: Manin pairs and moment maps revisited
arxiv-2404-17518.creator: Eckhard Meinrenken, Selim Tawfik
arxiv-2404-17518.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Eckhard Meinrenken, Selim Tawfik. The notion of quasi-Poisson G G -spaces with D / G D/G -valued moment maps was introduced by Alekseev and Kosmann-Schwarzbach in 1999. Our main result is a Lifting Theorem , establishing a bijective correspondence between the categories of quasi-Poisson G G -spaces with D / G D/G -valued moment maps and of quasi-Poisson G × G G\times G -spaces with D D -valued moment maps.

arxiv-2407-01323.title: Extending non-adiabatic rate theory to strong electronic couplings in the Marcus inverted regime
arxiv-2407-01323.creator: Thomas P. Fay
arxiv-2407-01323.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas P. Fay. Electron transfer reactions play an essential role in many chemical and biological processes. Fermi’s Golden rule, which assumes that the coupling between electronic states is small, has formed the foundation of electron transfer rate theory, however in short range electron/energy transfer reactions this coupling can become very large, and therefore Fermi’s Golden Rule fails to make even qualitatively accurate rate predictions.

arxiv-2412-14064.title: Oscillators with imaginary coupling: spectral functions in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory
arxiv-2412-14064.creator: Bruno W. Mintz, Itai Y. Pinheiro, Rui Aquino
arxiv-2412-14064.description: Abstract The axioms of Quantum Mechanics require that the hamiltonian of any closed system is self-adjoint, so that energy levels are real and time evolution preserves probability. On the other hand, non-hermitian hamiltonians with 𝒫𝒯 {\cal{PT}} -symmetry can have both real spectra and unitary time evolution.

arxiv-2503-18364.title: MaSS13K: A Matting-level Semantic Segmentation Benchmark
arxiv-2503-18364.creator: Chenxi Xie Minghan Li Hui Zeng Jun Luo Lei Zhang
arxiv-2503-18364.description: Abstract High-resolution semantic segmentation is essential for applications such as image editing, bokeh imaging, AR/VR, etc. Unfortunately, existing datasets often have limited resolution and lack precise mask details and boundaries. In this work, we build a large-scale, matting-level semantic segmentation dataset, named MaSS13K, which consists of 13,348 real-world images, all at 4K resolution.

arxiv-2509-20664.title: Enhancing Molecular Property Prediction with Knowledge from Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-20664.creator: Peng Zhou, Lai Hou Tim, Zhixiang Cheng, Kun Xie, Chaoyi Li, Wei Liu, Xiangxiang Zeng
arxiv-2509-20664.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Peng Zhou, Lai Hou Tim, Zhixiang Cheng, Kun Xie, Chaoyi Li, Wei Liu, Xiangxiang Zeng. Predicting molecular properties is a critical component of drug discovery. Recent advances in deep learning—particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)—have enabled end-to-end learning from molecular structures, reducing reliance on manual feature engineering. However, while GNNs and self-supervised learning approaches have advanced molecular property prediction (MPP), the integration of human prior knowledge remains indispensable, as evidenced by recent methods that leverage large language models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction.

arxiv-2510-16380.title: MoRe Bench : Evaluating Procedural and Pluralistic Mo ral Re asoning in Language Models, More than Outcomes
arxiv-2510-16380.creator: Yu Ying Chiu*, Michael S. Lee*, Rachel Calcott, Brandon Handoko, Paul de Font-Reaulx, Paula Rodriguez, Chen Bo Calvin Zhang, Ziwen Han✝, Udari Madhushani Sehwag, Yash Maurya, Christina Knight, Harry Lloyd, Florence Bacus, Mantas Mazeika, Bing Liu, Yejin Choi, Mitchell Gordon, Sydney Levine
arxiv-2510-16380.description: Abstract As AI systems progress, we rely more on them to make decisions with us and for us. To ensure that such decisions are aligned with human values, it is imperative for us to understand not only what decisions they make but also how they come to those decisions.

arxiv-2511-14163.title: Photon rest mass from localized fast radio bursts with improved distribution of dispersion measure from extragalactic gas
arxiv-2511-14163.creator: Yuchen Zhang, Yang Liu, Hongwei Yu, Puxun Wu
arxiv-2511-14163.description: Abstract The assumption that photons are massless is a foundational postulate of modern physics, yet it remains subject to experimental verification. Fast radio bursts (FRBs), with their cosmological distances and precisely measured dispersion, offer an excellent laboratory for testing this hypothesis.

This protocol is based on the use of type IIs restriction enzymes and

pmc-10632324.title: JAK-STAT signaling in inflammation and stress-related diseases: implications for therapeutic interventions
pmc-10632324.creator: Alexey Sarapultsev, Evgenii Gusev, Maria Komelkova, Irina Utepova, Shanshan Luo, Desheng Hu
pmc-10632324.description: The Janus kinase-signal transducer and transcription activator pathway (JAK-STAT) serves as a cornerstone in cellular signaling, regulating physiological and pathological processes such as inflammation and stress. Dysregulation in this pathway can lead to severe immunodeficiencies and malignancies, and its role extends to neurotransduction and pro-inflammatory signaling mechanisms.

pmc-11416509.title: DNA methylation changes in the genome of patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
pmc-11416509.creator: Erina Suzuki, Kazuhiko Nakabayashi, Saki Aoto, Tsutomu Ogata, Yoko Kuroki, Mami Miyado, Maki Fukami, Keiko Matsubara
pmc-11416509.description: Although some Mendelian neurodevelopmental disorders have been shown to entail specific DNA methylation changes designated as epi-signatures, it remains unknown whether epi-signatures are consistent features of other genetic disorders. Here, we analyzed DNA methylation profiles of patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HH), a rare neuroendocrine disorder typically caused by monogenic or oligogenic mutations.

pmc-13231775.title: Prevalence of temporomandibular disorders and their association with psychosocial and behavioural factors among medical and dental postgraduate residents: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13231775.creator: ShahrukhAli Khan, Hassan Yaqoob, Syeda Farah Jabeen, Taimur Khalid, Syed Murtaza Raza Kazmi
pmc-13231775.description: BackgroundTemporomandibular disorders (TMD) are multifactorial conditions influenced by biological, behavioral, and psychological factors. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of TMD and to examine its association with psycho-emotional factors and oral parafunctional behaviors among postgraduate medical and dental residents using the diagnostic criteria for Temporomandibular disorders (DC/TMD).

pmc-13318531.title: Sleep Deprivation and Neuronal Hyperexcitation Share Transcriptomic Signatures
pmc-13318531.creator: Markos Michail Chatzigiannis, Hideo Hagihara, Tsuyoshi Miyakawa
pmc-13318531.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Although sleep deprivation (SD) is clinically associated with numerous neuropsychiatric disorders, its underlying molecular correlates remain unclear. Because extended wakefulness is accompanied by increased neuronal activity and network firing, SD may be associated with a hyperactive neural state. This study aimed to test the hypothesis that SD shares transcriptomic signatures induced by neuronal hyperexcitation and to identify the gene pathways and cell types associated with these signatures. Publicly available transcriptomic datasets were analyzed, including 32 SD and 23 neuronal hyperexcitation transcriptomic datasets.
